chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is the limit of good character?' He said, 'You soften your wing, and make your speech sweet, and meet your brother with a pleasant smile.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics of good moral character in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distills the abstract concept of *husn al-khuluq* into tangible social etiquette, emphasizing that true nobility is manifested through approachability and warmth rather than mere status. This narration aligns with the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a spiritual discipline, where physical demeanor reflects inner moral refinement. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining harmonious community relations, reinforcing the idea that kindness is an active, visible practice.
